CodingQuestion.title: CodingQuestion
CodingQuestion.description: Represents a coding question from a specific platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CodingQuestion entity.

platformId.description: Reference to the CodingPlatform. (Relationship: CodingPlatform 1:N CodingQuestion)

link.description: Link to the coding question on the original platform.

difficulty.description: Difficulty level of the coding question (e.g., Easy, Medium, Hard).

CodingPlatform.title: CodingPlatform
CodingPlatform.description: Represents a coding platform (e.g., LeetCode, Codeforces).

id.description: Unique identifier for the CodingPlatform entity.

definition.description: Stores information about coding platforms (e.g., LeetCode, Codeforces).

params.name: platformId
params.description: Unique identifier for the coding platform.

definition.description: Stores coding questions from various platforms.

params.name: questionId
params.description: Unique identifier for the coding question.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to store coding platforms and coding questions. Since the application focuses on searching and displaying coding questions from different platforms, the structure prioritizes efficient retrieval and filtering of this data. The structure uses simple collections for coding platforms and coding questions. Authorization independence is not a major concern here as there is no user-specific or private data to consider, since there's no user or private related entities, so security rules are very basic and don't rely on denormalization. List operations are supported efficiently since each collection represents a single entity and are flat (no subcollections).
